To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
“the nervous system of all animal species displays a modular architecture, with a few highly connected areas acting as hubs, that facilitate the integration of segregated sensory information”.
the brain is organized into modules, which are connected to one another through hubs, and that this modular organization is present in all animals, from worms to human.

the nervous system is a complex network of interconnected neurons that displays a modular organization with hubs that are highly connected and abundant alternative processing paths that allow for the segregation and integration of sensory information.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the analysis of the anatomical architecture of the brain, and the implications of such architecture in the functional organization of sensory systems and the integration of multisensory information.
the study of brain function from the perspective of the anatomical organization.
the analysis of the structural properties of the nervous system and their relation with brain function.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the brain is organized in such a way that it allows for the emergence of complex behaviors, which are not predetermined by its architecture but, on the contrary, are the consequence of the dynamical properties of its anatomical substrate.
the brain is organized in a modular way, and this is a fundamental principle for understanding its function.
the nervous system is organized as a network of networks, where each network is a modular structure of highly connected hubs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
brain connectivity is a fundamental feature of the nervous system and that it is a key element in understanding the functional organization of brain circuits.
brain function can be explored from the anatomical connectivity.
brain networks are organized in a hierarchical manner, with a modular structure and a few highly interconnected regions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, by using complex network analysis, we can extract a number of fundamental properties of the brain’s anatomical connectivity.
the architecture of the connectivity of the brain is a key factor to understand the brain function.

, in spite of the huge differences among species in terms of size, number of neurons, and complexity, the nervous system has developed similar strategies for the integration of information from the environment.
